class: Any catalogue method that derives one value per underlying + expiry from per-contract attributes (tick size, lot size, strike gap) fails or returns a wrong value when that expiry mixes instrument kinds (options and futures) whose attribute differs.
mechanism: The method groups contracts by underlying and expiry only and treats a non-uniform attribute as bad data, but Zerodha lists NIFTY options at tick 0.05 and the NIFTY future at tick 0.1 on the same expiry date.

first_seen.where: W-006 branch worktree-agent-aff2767756260822f @ cbafb26, backend/ofo/instruments/catalogue.py Catalogue.tick_size()
first_seen.evidence: Independent verifier ran tick_size on the real fixture for NIFTY expiry 2026-09-29: ValueError 'inconsistent tick size ... [0.05, 0.1]'. No test called tick_size(), so the suite was green (16 passed).

fix: Tick and lot size derived per underlying + expiry + instrument kind (option vs future); merged with W-006.

detection.note: Per-kind derivation tested on the real fixture across every underlying+expiry+kind; independent verifier checked all 44 combinations on the full real list (2026-09-29). Related residual: far-from-money strikes jump by 1,300/1,500, so W-003 must place scenario columns on listed strikes.
